evals.prompt: $plan Produce an implementation-ready plan from the following complete synthetic accepted inputs; do not search for additional fixtures. Change Specification CS-27 revision 3 and Design D-27 revision 2 target current Implementation r140. Architecture A-API revision 2 maps to src/api/contracts.ts and src/api/router.ts; Architecture A-STORE revision 5 maps to src/store/port.ts and src/store/repository.ts, and API behavior depends on the store port. Requirement R-17 revision 1 requires invalid requests to be rejected before storage; Requirement R-18 revision 1 requires accepted writes to commit atomically. AP-4 revision 1 evaluates A-API via evals/architecture/api-boundary.ts after contracts and routing exist. AP-5 revision 1 evaluates A-STORE via evals/architecture/store-dependencies.ts after the port and repository exist. RP-8 revision 2 evaluates R-17 via evals/requirements/request-rejection.ts once the API seam and first rejection behavior exist. RP-9 revision 1 evaluates R-18 via evals/requirements/atomic-write.ts once the store seam and first write slice exist. All four are fast executable Protocols and must run after changes to their covered units and against the final candidate. r140 already contains the named units and evaluation harness; no schema migration is needed. Rollout uses a disabled-by-default feature flag and rollback disables the flag. Planning is authorized, and implementation mutation authority exists for the later handoff but must not be exercised in this run. Make the required Evaluations useful during behavioral realization as well as final exit criteria. Implementation-conformance Evaluations may remain delegated. Do not implement.
evals.expected_output: An implementation-ready evidence-guided plan that sequences architecture-bearing prerequisites before dependent behavior, realizes required Protocols at their earliest useful points, repeatedly executes them as implementation feedback, and requires final evidence against the exact candidate revision.
assertions: The exact Change, Change Specification, Change Design, current Implementation, Architecture, Requirement, and required Protocol identities are bound.

Architecture-bearing boundaries, contracts, ownership, observability, and testability seams precede behavior that depends on them unless an explicit compatibility, migration, or atomicity dependency requires interleaving.

Every required Requirement-satisfaction and Architecture-realization Protocol has an executable realization, earliest meaningful execution point, re-execution trigger or cadence, Result-driven continue/stop/return behavior, and final candidate-revision execution.
Required Protocol Executions guide bounded behavioral increments instead of appearing only as terminal checks.

Final Requirement-satisfaction and Architecture-realization evidence is an exit condition bound to the exact candidate revision without claiming that planning or implementation itself establishes satisfaction or realization.
Implementation-conformance Evaluations remain a separate delegated choice unless an accepted input requires them.
No implementation starts.
